sentences.text: Verify STXBP1 membership in Neurotransmitter release cycle (stability 1.00).

sentences.text: Verify the counterexample GNAO1-related disease (neurodevelopmental disorder with involuntary movements): clinical similarity P=0.98, mechanism M=0.00; it is excluded by the mechanism layer.
Verify CACNA1A-related disease (migraine, familial hemiplegic, 1): 1 shared process term(s) (Regulation of insulin secretion; R-HSA-422356); M=0.11, S=0.40, excluded by M layer.
Verify SLC2A1-related disease (hereditary cryohydrocytosis with reduced stomatin): 1 shared process term(s) (Regulation of insulin secretion; R-HSA-422356); M=0.08, S=0.49, excluded by M layer.

Verify GRIN1-related disease (neurodevelopmental disorder with or without hyperkinetic movements and seizures, autosomal dominant): 1 shared process term(s) (Neurexins and neuroligins; R-HSA-6794361); M=0.06, S=0.45, excluded by M layer.
Verify DNM1-related disease (developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 31B): 1 shared process term(s) (vesicle organization; GO:0016050); M=0.03, S=0.51, excluded by M layer.

Verify V=0 against CACNA1A-related disease (migraine, familial hemiplegic, 1): STXBP1 is loss_of_function (“De novo loss of function mutations in STXBP1 are a relatively common cause of epilepsy and intellectual disability (ID).”); the comparator is gain_of_function (“Two variants known leading to gain of function (GOF) were found in 5 patients.”).

Verify V=0 against GRIN1-related disease (neurodevelopmental disorder with or without hyperkinetic movements and seizures, autosomal dominant): STXBP1 is loss_of_function (“De novo loss of function mutations in STXBP1 are a relatively common cause of epilepsy and intellectual disability (ID).”); the comparator is gain_of_function (“including variants in the pore-forming region, linker regions and elsewhere that uniformly increase NMDA receptor-mediated charge transfer.”).
Contradictory evidence is indexed: “We found no correlation between severity of seizures and severity of ID”.
Contradictory evidence is indexed: “or between mutation type and seizure characteristics or cognitive outcome.”.

Contradictory evidence is indexed: “None of the recurrent variants were significantly associated with distinct electroclinical syndromes, single phenotypic features, or showed overall clinical similarity”.

Verify Ingo Helbig with DNM1-related disease (developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 31B): matching ORCID 0000000184860558; CT.gov official affiliation match "Children's Hospital of Philadelphia" / "The Children's Hospital of Philadelphia"; overlapping affiliation tokens [albrechts, christian] at 'Christian Albrechts University of Kiel and University Medical Center Schleswig-Holstein (UKSH)' and 'Christian-Albrechts-University'; shared co-author 'Elizabeth Palmer' on PMID:35851549 and PMID:28667181.

Verify Sarah McKeown Ruggiero with DNM1-related disease (developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 31B): matching ORCID 0000000208340750; overlapping affiliation tokens [children, philadelphia] at "Children's Hospital of Philadelphia" and "Children's Hospital of Philadelphia"; shared co-author 'Ingo Helbig' on PMID:35851549 and PMID:36413998.

Verify Katherine L Helbig with DNM1-related disease (developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 31B): matching ORCID 0000000182490549; overlapping affiliation tokens [aliso, ambry, california] at 'Division of Clinical Genomics, Ambry Genetics, Aliso Viejo, California, USA' and 'Division of Clinical Genomics, Ambry Genetics, Aliso Viejo, California, USA'; shared co-author 'Deepali N Shinde' on PMID:26795593 and PMID:28667181.

Verify STXBP1 and SYNGAP1 Related Disorders Natural History Study (NCT06555965) eligibility for DNM1-related disease (developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 31B) and confirm Ingo Helbig using matching ORCID 0000000184860558; CT.gov official affiliation match "Children's Hospital of Philadelphia" / "The Children's Hospital of Philadelphia"; overlapping affiliation tokens [albrechts, christian] at 'Christian Albrechts University of Kiel and University Medical Center Schleswig-Holstein (UKSH)' and 'Christian-Albrechts-University'; shared co-author 'Elizabeth Palmer' on PMID:35851549 and PMID:28667181.
